name: ARMM
summary_text: ARMM (predecessor to BARMM) is the only unit where a structurally different legal system applies to a visitor in conflict situations. The Bangsamoro Administrative Code (BAA-13, 2019) provides that justice in the autonomous region shall be dispensed "in consonance with the Constitution, Shari'ah, traditional or tribal laws." Parliament Bill No. 473 (July 2026) proposes a comprehensive Bangsamoro Shari'ah Justice System Code adding ta'zir criminal offences—the category under which morality offences against same-sex conduct and gender expression are prosecuted in comparable systems. Nationally, the Shari'ah court system is expanding: President Marcos Jr. signed a law in August 2024 creating three new Shari'ah judicial districts beyond BARMM, RA 12304 (September 2025) ensures equitable access, and the Supreme Court resolved in January 2026 to operationalise the Shari'ah High Court. The dossier's assessor caveat is explicit: no source establishes that Philippine Shari'ah courts currently prosecute same-sex conduct or gender expression, and the original P.D. 1083 codified only personal law. The finding is structural—a jurisdiction with an active legislative process to create criminal religious law, in a region where a visitor's dispute may be adjudicated outside the Philippine court system entirely—rather than a documented enforcement reality. Net effect: −0.07 below the national score. The risk is forward-looking and legal-framework-based, not enforcement-based, which limits the deviation under the "enforcement > statute" rule. However, the ta'zir drafting is the single most severe structural threat identified in the dossier for a transgender visitor, and the absence of any protective ordinance or civil-rights infrastructure in ARMM means no counterweight exists. Compare CAR (0.54), which also has a legal-pluralism concern but no criminal-law component.

sources.claim_summary: Full text of Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 13 (the Bangsamoro Administrative Code), begun 29 March 2019, from the Bangsamoro Official Gazette: prescribes the structures and rules of governance of the autonomous region (cached extract covers the introductory provisions; the code's justice-dispensation clause — 'in consonance with the Constitution, Shari'ah, traditional or tribal laws' — is cited in the dossier), while guaranteeing religious freedom.

sources.title: Proposed Bangsamoro Shari’ah Justice System Code seeks broader legal framework for Shari’ah justice | Bangsamoro Parliament
sources.claim_summary: Bangsamoro Parliament release (14 July 2026): Parliament Bill No. 473 proposes a comprehensive Bangsamoro Shari'ah Justice System Code governing Shari'ah civil actions, Islamic commercial transactions, supplementary Muslim family relations, ta'zir offences, alternative dispute resolution and Agama arbitration; ta'zir is the Sharia criminal category under which morality offences against same-sex conduct and gender expression are prosecuted in comparable systems (cached page body largely site navigation).

sources.title: Evangelicals Divided as Sharia Courts Expand in the Philippines - Christianity Today
sources.claim_summary: Christianity Today report (November 2024): in August 2024 President Ferdinand 'Bongbong' Marcos Jr. signed a law creating three new Shari'ah judicial districts and twelve circuit courts, spreading the Islamic court system beyond BARMM into majority-Christian areas of Mindanao, the Visayas, Luzon and Metro Manila; most evangelical leaders learned of it months later; the Shari'ah system was originally established in 1977 by Marcos Sr.

sources.title: P.D. No. 1083
sources.claim_summary: Full text of Presidential Decree No. 1083 (1977), the Code of Muslim Personal Laws of the Philippines: creates Shari'ah District and Circuit Courts as courts of limited jurisdiction within the Philippine judicial system under Supreme Court supervision, applying only to Muslims, and codifying personal law — personal status, marriage and divorce, matrimonial and family relations, succession and inheritance — not criminal offences.
